name: Setmelanotide
status: FDA-approved for rare genetic obesity (2020), Bardet-Biedl syndrome (2022) and acquired hypothalamic obesity (2026)
mechanism: Activates the melanocortin-4 receptor in the hypothalamus, restoring a fullness signal that is broken in certain genetic and brain-injury forms of obesity
uses: Obesity from POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency

article.summary: Setmelanotide (Imcivree) is a daily injection that restores a brain fullness signal. It is FDA-approved for rare genetic obesity, Bardet-Biedl syndrome and acquired hypothalamic obesity.
article.takeaway: Setmelanotide is a precision obesity drug: it works only where the problem lies in one specific appetite pathway in the brain, the leptin-melanocortin system. In people with POMC deficiency, **8 of 10 lost at least 10% of their weight** in about a year, and extreme hunger eased.[^1] In acquired hypothalamic obesity, usually caused by brain tumors or their treatment, BMI fell **16.5% versus a 3.3% rise on placebo**.[^2] It is not meant for common obesity, and skin darkening is one of its most frequent side effects.[^3]
glance: POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency; Bardet-Biedl syndrome; acquired hypothalamic obesity
Injection under the skin once a day
Small open-label and placebo-controlled phase 3 trials in rare conditions

blocks.text: Fat tissue releases leptin, which tells the hypothalamus how much energy the body has stored. Leptin acts through a relay: nerve cells make POMC, which is cut by the enzyme PCSK1 into melanocortin hormones, which then switch on the melanocortin-4 (MC4) receptor to signal fullness. When any link in that chain is broken, people feel relentless hunger (hyperphagia) and gain weight from early childhood.

Setmelanotide is an eight-amino-acid ring peptide that activates MC4 receptors directly, bypassing the broken steps. Because it also touches the related MC1 receptor on pigment cells, it tends to darken the skin.

items: **Monogenic obesity (ages 2 and up):** POMC, PCSK1 or LEPR deficiency confirmed by genetic testing
**Bardet-Biedl syndrome (ages 2 and up):** a rare inherited disorder that affects vision, kidneys and appetite
**Acquired hypothalamic obesity (ages 4 and up):** weight gain after damage to the hypothalamus, often from tumors such as craniopharyngioma or their surgery or radiation

blocks.text: The label states that it is not expected to work for general obesity or for other genetic syndromes, and that harmless gene variants do not qualify.[^3]

rows: 21 people aged 6+ with POMC or LEPR deficiency
38 people with BBS or Alström syndrome
10%+ weight loss in 32% of BBS patients aged 12+[^4]
120 people aged 4-66 with acquired hypothalamic obesity
BMI -16.5% vs +3.3% on placebo; hunger scores fell more[^2]

blocks.text: Because these conditions are rare, the first trials were small and partly open-label. TRANSCEND, published in 2026, was a larger randomized, placebo-controlled study.

Setmelanotide is injected under the skin once a day. Starting doses depend on age and condition, typically 0.5-2 mg for two weeks, and are raised toward a 3 mg maintenance dose for most people aged 6 and older. Younger children's doses are based on body weight, and kidney problems call for adjustments.[^3]

items: **Very common:** skin darkening, darkening of existing moles and new moles, so a full skin exam is advised before and during treatment
**Common:** injection-site reactions, nausea, vomiting and headache
**Sexual effects:** spontaneous erections in males (seek care for one lasting over 4 hours) and sexual side effects in females
**Mood:** depression and suicidal thoughts have occurred and should be monitored
**Hypothalamic obesity:** watch for adrenal crisis and sodium swings in people with central diabetes insipidus[^3]

evidence.label: Approved: small but consistent trials in rare diseases
evidence.text: Evidence comes from small single-arm trials in genetic obesity and placebo-controlled trials in Bardet-Biedl syndrome and hypothalamic obesity.[^1][^4][^2] Effects are large in the right patients, but long-term outcomes beyond a few years are still being collected.

faq.q: Can setmelanotide be used for ordinary obesity?
faq.a: No. It is designed for people whose obesity comes from a defect in the MC4 pathway or hypothalamic damage. For common obesity, drugs such as [semaglutide](/peptides/semaglutide) and [tirzepatide](/peptides/tirzepatide) are used instead.

faq.q: How do I know if I have one of the qualifying conditions?
faq.a: Monogenic forms are confirmed by genetic testing, Bardet-Biedl syndrome by clinical features and genetics, and hypothalamic obesity by a history of hypothalamic injury followed by weight gain. A specialist can help decide whether testing makes sense.

faq.q: Why does setmelanotide darken the skin?
faq.a: Besides MC4, it activates MC1 receptors on pigment cells, the receptor involved in tanning. The label advises full skin exams before and during treatment to track existing and new moles.[^3]
